3662890.background: São Paulo elects two senators; Mara Gabrilli and Alexandre Giordano hold the seats. Marina Silva (Rede), environment minister and SP federal deputy, is a Lula-camp candidate. Governor Tarcísio's right coalition fields strong names (e.g., Guilherme Derrite); left needs to concentrate votes.

actors.name: Marina Silva (Rede)
actors.public: Environment minister, ex-presidential candidate, nationally known; ~238k votes as SP deputy 2022.
actors.private: Will accept Lula-bloc second slot; needs PT voters to give her their second vote.

actors.name: Tarcísio / right coalition
actors.public: Popular governor; likely pair such as Derrite (PP) plus a PL name.
actors.private: A disciplined two-name right slate could take both seats.

actors.name: PT / Lula bloc
actors.public: May run its own name (e.g., Haddad, Simone Tebet, Márcio França) alongside Marina.
actors.private: Two left names split ~45% of vote.

actors.name: Bolsonaro family / PL
actors.public: Eduardo Bolsonaro's situation abroad; PL wants a Senate name.
actors.private: PL choices could split right vote.

events.name: Marina withdraws or switches to other office
A third strong right candidate splits the vote

3662925.background: Tocantins elects two senators; Eduardo Gomes (PL) and Irajá (PSD) hold seats. Federal deputy Alexandre Guimarães runs. Governor Wanderlei Barbosa was removed by STJ in 2025 amid corruption probes, reshaping coalitions.

actors.name: Alexandre Guimarães
actors.public: Federal deputy; Senate candidate with regional base.
actors.private: Needs coalition slot; competes with incumbents for second place.

actors.name: Eduardo Gomes (PL)
actors.public: Incumbent senator, influential in Congress.
actors.private: Likely PL lead name.

actors.name: Irajá (PSD)
actors.public: Incumbent senator, son of Kátia Abreu.
actors.private: May seek re-election or governor.

actors.name: State government factions
actors.public: Power contested after Barbosa's removal.
actors.private: Machine support decisive.

events.name: Dorinha or Kátia Abreu enters Senate race

3663126.background: Amapá's first-round presidential vote. In 2022 Bolsonaro narrowly led Lula in Amapá in both rounds. Lula seeks re-election; Bolsonaro is ineligible and imprisoned, with Flávio Bolsonaro the PL candidate. Senate president Davi Alcolumbre (Amapá) has cooperated with Lula's government.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent president, strong in North/Northeast; federal programs (Bolsa Família) important in Amapá.
actors.private: Wants to flip Amapá; relies on Alcolumbre and local allies.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: PL presidential candidate inheriting Bolsonaro's base.
actors.private: Weaker than his father with moderates; evangelical vote key in Amapá.

actors.name: Davi Alcolumbre (União)
actors.public: Senate president, dominant Amapá politician.
actors.private: Pragmatic; local machine effort for Lula uncertain.

actors.name: Other right candidates (e.g., Ratinho Jr, Caiado, Zema)
actors.public: Fragment the anti-Lula vote.
actors.private: Fragmentation helps Lula top the first round.

3663206.background: Ceará's first-round presidential vote. Lula won ~66% in Ceará in 2022 first round. Ceará is governed by PT (Elmano de Freitas); Camilo Santana is a minister. Ciro Gomes joined PSDB and may run for governor. Flávio Bolsonaro is PL presidential candidate.

actors.name: Lula (PT)
actors.public: Incumbent president; dominant in Northeast.
actors.private: Expects large margin; key base.

actors.name: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)
actors.public: PL presidential candidate.
actors.private: Aims to reduce margin.

actors.name: Ciro Gomes / Ceará opposition
actors.public: Anti-PT alliance with right in state.
actors.private: Could raise opposition turnout.

actors.name: PT state machine (Elmano, Camilo)
actors.public: Controls state.
actors.private: Mobilizes for Lula.
